name: pi · What is the agent doing over time?
description: Tool activity per time bucket, split by category (git, tests, file edits, search). Tall bars of a single colour mean the agent is grinding on one kind of work.

name: pi · Where does shell time go?
description: Share of shell commands by category. A large 'other' slice means commands aren't being classified yet and the categories need widening.

name: pi · Which skills actually get loaded?
description: How often each skill file is read. Skills that never appear are dead weight in the prompt and can be removed.

name: pi · Which subagents do the work?
description: Share of delegated work per subagent. Heavy use of expensive agents for simple jobs is the main cost leak worth fixing.

name: pi · Which tools are slowest?
description: 95th-percentile duration per tool: 19 out of 20 calls finish faster than this. The top entries are where wall-clock time goes.

name: pi · Which tools fail, and how often?
description: Tool calls split by outcome. Anything with a high ERROR count is a broken workflow or a badly worded instruction.

name: pi · What am I spending, and on which model?
description: Hourly spend per model in USD. Sustained lines from an expensive model usually mean work that a cheaper one could have done.

name: pi · How fast does each model start replying?
description: 95th-percentile time to first token per model. High values are felt directly as lag before the agent responds.

name: pi · Is prompt caching working?
description: Share of input tokens served from cache, per model. Close to 1.0 is healthy; a drop means the prompt prefix changed and cache is being rebuilt — the most common source of silent cost increases.

name: pi · Did my last AGENTS.md change help?
description: Tool success rate per version of your instruction files. Compare bars before and after an edit: higher is better. Needs a few sessions per version before it means anything.

name: pi · Did my last AGENTS.md change make runs longer?
description: Average turns per session for each version of your instruction files. Lower usually means clearer instructions — unless the work itself got harder.

name: pi · Spend
description: Total spend across all agent runs in the selected period.

name: pi · Cache hit rate
description: Average share of input tokens served from cache. Below ~0.8 is worth investigating.

name: pi · Tool success rate
description: Share of tool calls that succeeded. Dips mean the agent is fighting its tools.

name: pi · Tool calls
description: Total tool calls in the period — a rough proxy for how much work the agent did.

name: pi · Context compactions
description: How often sessions ran out of context and had to compact. Frequent compaction means context is being wasted and cache is being invalidated.

name: pi · Cache hit rate over time
description: Cache efficiency over time. A cliff edge marks the moment a prompt or instruction change started invalidating the cache.
